title: fpextract floor-plan extraction (per image)
description: Tool-use input_schema forced on the vision model. One image may show multiple unit types (e.g. mirrored 'A1 / A1m' on one sheet); always return units as a list, even with a single unit. For non-unit-plan images (site_map, facility_plan, other), units must be an empty array.

classification.description: unit_plan = one or more residential units shown in plan view (room-level detail), no unit numbers visible; hybrid = single sheet with BOTH the storey/site-map layout AND per-unit room-level floor plans, with unit numbers visible (e.g. 'C8 02-06 to 08-06') — populate both `units` and `unit_number_map`; site_map = top-down block layout with unit numbers but NO room-level detail inside each cell; facility_plan = pool/gym/BBQ etc.; other = anything else (logos, key plans, marketing illustrations).

confidence.description: Your confidence in this extraction overall.

notes.description: Optional free text. Anything you noticed but couldn't fit into the structured fields.

unit_number_map.description: Maps individual unit numbers (e.g. '05-12', '#05-12') to their unit_type labels (e.g. 'B1', 'C8', 'A1-G'). Populate whenever unit numbers are visible ANYWHERE on the sheet — regardless of classification. Sources include cell labels in site-map / hybrid layouts, comma-separated lists under a unit-type heading on a unit_plan sheet (e.g. 'Unit #02-22, #04-12, #04-14'), and stack-view tables at the bottom of the sheet (rows = storeys, columns = positions, each cell prints both unit number and unit_type). One key per unit number — NEVER a range. Range labels like 'C8 02-06 to 08-06' on a 2nd-to-8th-storey sheet are expanded into one key per storey: {'02-06': 'C8', '03-06': 'C8', ..., '08-06': 'C8'}. Use the unit-number format exactly as drawn (keep '#' prefix or block prefix like 'B1-#02-03' if printed). Leave empty only when no unit numbers appear anywhere on the sheet.

units.description: One entry per distinct unit floor shown on the sheet. Empty array if classification != unit_plan.

unit_type.description: As labelled on the drawing, e.g. '2BR Type B1', 'Penthouse PH3'. Use 'Unknown' if unlabelled.

floor_label.description: Used in two scenarios — disambiguate by the value you write. (1) Multi-storey units (duplex, penthouse, maisonette): which floor of the unit this plan represents, e.g. 'Lower Floor', 'Upper Floor'. Two entries sharing unit_type but with different floor_label values are floors of the same unit. (2) Typical floor plate sheets: which storey range of the building this unit belongs to, e.g. '2nd Storey', '3rd-11th Storey'. Same unit_type appearing on different storey rows with layout differences gets a separate entry per row.

total_area_sqm.description: Strata / total area as printed on the drawing.

facing.description: Compass direction the main living area faces, derived from the drawing's North arrow.

rooms.description: Semantic room list — names and areas only, no geometry.

label.description: Room label exactly as printed, e.g. 'Master Bedroom', 'Bath 2', 'A/C Ledge'.

windows.description: One entry per window. Room name and which wall it is on.

crop_frac.description: [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max] as fractions of the image dimensions (0 = left/top edge, 1 = right/bottom edge). Tight bounding box around ONE instance of this unit_type — include its walls, room labels, dimension annotations, and immediately-adjacent compass/scale; exclude the unit-type title block, area legend, watermarks, tower-locator insets, and neighbouring cells of any other unit_type. Hard constraints: (1) coordinates must stay inside the drawn area — never extend into empty page margin or past the building footprint; (2) two crop_frac values for different unit_types must not overlap by area, only meet along their shared boundary at most; (3) when the same unit_type appears in multiple cells on a typical-floor-plate / hybrid sheet, pick the clearest single instance and crop only that cell — don't span multiple instances or include corridors between them. unit_number_map records where every numbered instance lives; crop_frac is the visual for one of them.
